name: Learn basic clay sculpting
blurb: Hand-building with clay teaches you to think in three dimensions. Pinch pots, coils and slabs are three techniques that between them make almost anything.
gear: Air-dry clay or polymer clay to start
Simple tools: a wire, a rib, a loop tool
A board and a damp cloth
steps: Learn to wedge the clay — kneading out air bubbles — because trapped air ruins pieces, especially if you ever fire them.
Make a pinch pot: a ball opened with your thumb and walls thinned evenly. It teaches wall thickness by feel.
Learn coil building for taller forms, scoring and slipping every join.
Learn slab building for angular forms, and how to let slabs firm up before assembly.
Sculpt a simple figure or head, building up an armature if the form needs support.
Learn to finish: smoothing, texturing, and drying slowly under plastic to prevent cracks.
tips: Uneven wall thickness causes cracks as it dries. Aim for consistency.
Score and slip every join, every time, or it will separate.
Drying too fast is the usual cause of cracks. Slow it down with plastic.
proof: A finished piece using all three techniques that dries without cracking.
